message.content:
**Answer:** One of the most celebrated and widely recognized sculptures of the 19th century is **“The Kiss” (Le Baiser)** by French artist **Auguste Rodin**, completed in 1889. --- ### Why “The Kiss” stands out | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Artist** | Auguste Rodin (1840‑1917) – often called the father of modern sculpture. | | **Date** | 1889 (first cast; subsequent editions produced later). | | **Material** | Bronze (originally marble, later bronze casts). | | **Dimensions** | Roughly 1.5 m × 1.5 m (varies by edition). | | **Style** | Realist/Impressionist blend; dynamic movement, textured surfaces, emotional intensity. | | **Iconography** | A couple locked in an intimate embrace, head tilted, hands intertwined—capturing both tenderness and tension. | | **Cultural Impact** | • Became a symbol of romantic love and artistic freedom.
• Inspired countless reproductions, parodies, and homages worldwide.
• Frequently displayed in major museums (e.g., Musée Rodin, Paris; National Gallery of Art, Washington D.C.). | --- ### Context within the 19th‑Century Sculpture Scene - **Rodin’s Innovation**: He broke away from classical idealism, focusing on psychological depth and naturalistic detail. “The Kiss” exemplifies this shift toward expressive realism. - **Contemporaries**: While other notable works emerged (e.g., “The Gates of Hell,” “The Thinker”—the latter finished in 1902), “The Kiss” captured public imagination during its time and remains instantly recognizable today. - **Legacy**: It set a precedent for modern sculpture, influencing artists such as Constantin Brâncuși and Henry Moore. --- ### Quick Reference - **Title**: *The Kiss* (Le Baiser) - **Artist**: Auguste Rodin - **Year Completed**: 1889 - **Medium**: Bronze (originally marble) - **Location(s)**: Musée Rodin (Paris), National Gallery of Art (Washington D.C.), many public parks and museums worldwide. --- **Bottom line:** If you’re looking for a single sculpture that epitomizes fame, influence, and enduring appeal from the 19th century, “The Kiss” by Rodin is the quintessential choice.
